interest: Shows postwar Wall Street firms probing Korean and Japanese banking rules, zaibatsu dissolution, and the new Korean Foreign Exchange Bank.
keywords: Financial Institutions Reconstruction and Reorganization Law
overview: This file comprises correspondence from July and August 1947 between the Irving Trust Company of New York, the Department of Commerce, and the Department of State's Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs concerning the operating conditions and foreign exchange status of commercial banks in occupied Japan and post-liberation Korea. Prompted by inquiries from Irving Trust Vice President F. Hartman regarding the resumption of international banking operations and the specific statuses of the Yasuda Bank in Tokyo and the newly established Korean Foreign Exchange Bank in Seoul, State Department official Roswell H. Whitman provides a comprehensive explanation of Allied occupation policies under SCAP and the U.S. Military Government in Korea. The documents detail the severance of external assets, currency conversion and deposit-blocking initiatives under Japan's Emergency Financial Measures and the Financial Institutions Reconstruction and Reorganization Law of 1946, the classification of Yasuda Bank as a restricted zaibatsu affiliate under Imperial Ordinance No. 657, and the institutional setup of Korea's nascent foreign exchange mechanism pending economic stabilization.

subfiles.about: Irving Trust Company inquires with the State Department regarding operating regulations, foreign exchange plans, and the status of native banks in Korea and Japan, particularly the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank.
subfiles.summary: Irving Trust's Hartman asks Edwin Martin about Korean banking conditions, foreign exchange prospects, and the newly operating Korean Foreign Exchange Bank, Ltd. in Seoul.
subfiles.title: Letter from F. Hartman (Irving Trust Company) to Edwin M. Martin regarding banking and foreign exchange in Korea and Japan

subfiles.about: The Department of Commerce informs Irving Trust Company that its inquiry regarding Japanese banking conditions and Yasuda Bank has been referred to the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: Commerce's Moser tells Hartman that Japanese banking falls under SCAP policy, so his inquiry on Japanese banking, exchange, and Yasuda Bank is referred to State's Edwin Martin.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles K. Moser (Department of Commerce) to F. Hartman referring inquiry on Japanese banking to Department of State

subfiles.about: The Department of State outlines operating regulations, financial reorganization measures, and foreign exchange restrictions affecting Japanese and Korean banks, including Yasuda Bank and the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank.
keywords: Financial Institutions Reconstruction and Reorganization Law
subfiles.summary: Whitman details postwar Japanese and Korean banking restrictions: domestic-only business, barred foreign exchange, Japan's Financial Institutions Reconstruction Law splitting accounts, Yasuda Bank's restricted zaibatsu status, and the new Korean Foreign Exchange Bank for trade documents.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman (Department of State) to F. Hartman on banking and foreign exchange regulations in Japan and Korea
